'''Levon Vrami Harutyunyan''' (Armenian: Լևոն Վռամի Հարությունյան; 13 December 1927 – 2007) was an Armenian biologist, University Professor, journalist, publicist, writer and science populariser, founder of [[Haybusak University of Yerevan|Yerevan Haybusak University]]. Established in 1990, the Haybusak University became one of the first private universities in [[Armenia]].<ref>{{cite news|script-title=hy:Երևանի «Հայբուսակ» համալասարան|url=http://armuniversity.com/index.php/en/studying-in-armenia/private-universities/281--lr-.html|website=ArmUniversity|language=hy|trans-title=Haybusak University of Yerevan |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015183145/http://armuniversity.com/index.php/en/studying-in-armenia/private-universities/281--lr-.html|archive-date=October 15, 2014}}</ref> He received numerous decorations for his work including [[Anania Shirakatsi]] medal from the [[President of Armenia]].

==Life and career==
Levon Vrami Harutyunyan was born 13 December 1927 in the village of [[Tavush (village)|Tovuz]] in the [[Tavush Province]] of [[Soviet Armenia]].<ref name=harutyunyan>{{cite journal|title=Levon Harutyunyan|journal=Armenian Concise Encyclopedia|date=2003|volume=1|page=320|url=https://hy.wikisource.org/wiki/%D4%B7%D5%BB:%D5%80%D5%A1%D5%B5%D5%AF%D5%A1%D5%AF%D5%A1%D5%B6_%D5%80%D5%A1%D5%B4%D5%A1%D5%BC%D5%B8%D5%BF_%D5%80%D5%A1%D5%B6%D6%80%D5%A1%D5%A3%D5%AB%D5%BF%D5%A1%D6%80%D5%A1%D5%B6%E2%80%A4_%D5%80_%D5%BF%D5%A1%D5%BC%D5%B8%D5%BE_%D5%B0%D5%B8%D5%A4%D5%BE%D5%A1%D5%AE%D5%B6%D5%A5%D6%80%D5%A8.djvu/288|language=hy}}</ref>

Harutyunyan studied and graduated from the Armenian Agricultural Institute (now known as [[Armenian National Agrarian University]]) in 1953.<ref name=harutyunyan/> From 1956 to 1978, Harutyunyan worked at the National Academy of Sciences under its botany department.<ref name=harutyunyan/> Meanwhile, in 1971, he became a member of the Union of Journalists of Armenia.<ref name=founder/> In 1990, he founded the Yerevan "Haybusak" Institute (now Yerevan "2Haybusak" University) upon which he became leading [[Rector (academia)|rector]].<ref name=founder/> Thereafter, in 1994, he became the president of the scientific-educational association "Harutyun".<ref name=founder/> In 1995, Harutyunyan became the head chairman of Biology and Biology Teaching Methods at the [[Armenian State Pedagogical University|Yerevan State Pedagogical University]]. In 2006, he was nominated as the President of International Academy of Education. He was the head of the department of science within the academy.<ref name=founder/>

{{quote box
| width  = 15%
| align  = right
| quote  = "I've done what I could. Let others do even more so."
| source = Levon Harutyunyan<ref>{{cite news|script-title=hy:'ՙԵՍ ԱՐԵՑԻ, ԻՆՉ ԿԱՐՈՂ ԷԻ, ԹՈՂ ՈՒՐԻՇՆԵՐՆ ԱՎԵԼԻՆ ԱՆԵՆ...՚'|url=http://www.iravunk.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=4090:2012-04-04-19-36-17&catid=53:hanrutyun&Itemid=176|agency=Iravunk|date=14 December 2014|language=hy |url-status=dead|trans-title=I Did What I Could, Let Others Do More |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017140909/http://www.iravunk.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=4090:2012-04-04-19-36-17&catid=53:hanrutyun&Itemid=176|archive-date=October 17, 2014}}</ref>}}

Harutyunyan authored more than 400 research papers, about 400 essays, non-scientific journal articles, over 50 monographs, handbooks, method manuals and dictionaries.<ref name=founder>{{cite web|script-title=hy:Մեր հիմնադիրը|url=http://www.academedu.org/ancnakazm/mer|website=International Academy of Education|language=hy|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201215719/http://academedu.org/ancnakazm/mer|archivedate=2015-02-01 |trans-title=Our Founder : LEVON HARUTYUNYAN}}</ref> His notable publications (via Haybusak University Press) include ''Phytotherapy'', ''Entertaining Botany'', ''A Journey to the Hiding Places of Nature'', ''The Nature of Armenia and Ways of its Preservation and Enrichment'', and ''The Gardener's Encyclopaedia''. He was involved with the landscaping of Yerevan and has authored several books on landscape preservation.<ref name=harutyunyan/>

==Family==
Harutyunyan and his wife Silva Aslikian had two daughters (Anahit and Anna) and one son (Suren).<ref>{{cite news|last1=Մելքոնյան|first1=Արմենուհի|script-title=hy:Մի կյանքի պատմություն. 20-ամյա «Հայբուսակ»-ի հիմնադիր Լեւոն Հարությունյանի գործերի ցուցահանդեսը|url=http://www.hayary.org/wph/?p=2033|agency=Լուսանցք|date=2011|language=hy|trans-title=A life story. The exhibition of the works of the 20-year-old founder of "Haybusak" Levon Harutyunyan}}</ref>

==Awards and titles==
Among some of Harutyunyan's awards and titles include:<ref name=founder/>
*2007 – Member of [[International Informatization Academy]] (www.iia.ca)
*2003 – Anania Shirakatsi Gold Medal awarded by the President of RA
*2002 – Member of International Pedagogical Academy
*1983 – Award by State TV and Radio Emissions Committee. Award by the Republican Nature Preservation Council
*1983 – Title of Professor
*1971 – Member of the Union of Journalists of Armenia
*1970 – Doctor of Biology thesis defense
*1961 – PhD thesis defense

==Publications==
Some of his publications include:
*"Hayastani Dendrofloran". Yerevan. 1985. Luis hratarakchutyun (in Armenian)
*"Partizagortsi hanragitaran". Nahapet hrat. Haybusak hratarak. Yerevan 2005 (in Armenian)
*"Arcaxi Floran". Yerevan, 2007, Nahapet hrat (in Armenian)
